Issued at 227 AM EDT Thu Aug 20 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

596dm upper ridge over the western US...with a 546dm upper low near 
James Bay and attendant broad troughing across Eastern Canada oozing 
influence into the northeastern US, including the Great Lakes...with 
4-8C 850mb air just to our north attm. A handful of perturbations in 
the flow over the PacNW and southern Canadian Prairies, with a 
notable PV maximum digging through the Mid MS Valley. Deepest 
moisture is generally focused near and south of the OH Valley along 
a baroclinic zone stretching from the central Plains to the Lower 
Great Lakes, where pwats again approach 1.5in or better, generally 
down to the Gulf Coast, with another BCZ draped from OK to SC. There 
is, however, a N-S oriented plume of moisture from Saskatchewan down 
into the Upper Midwest, attendant to aforementioned perturbations 
and surface reflection stretching from northern Saskatchewan down 
into the northern Plains...with some warm advection convection north 
of the US/Canada border and trying to sneak into the tip of MN. For 
now, the Great Lakes remains generally under the influence of high 
pressure in the wake of aforementioned OH Valley baroclinic 
zone...with generally cooler and less humid conditions compared to 
previous days as prevailing surface flow (albeit light) is broadly 
northerly. 

Subtle ridging briefly takes hold today...but will look for upstream 
PV max over southern Canada to head our way later today into 
tonight, which could bring a shot at some activity to the region. 
This should exit stage right Friday...though upstream niblets of PV 
look to dig into the OH Valley and reinforce the troughing/unsettled 
idea to wrap up the work week. Currently expecting energy to dig 
south into the Great Lakes Saturday and Saturday night as trough 
axis sharpens over the region; expect this will bring some 
showers/storms as well, which could linger into Sunday with signals 
for additional energy to further reinforce the trough idea over the 
region, and northerly flow should overtake the area as high pressure 
attempts to build in from the west/northwest. Upper low currently 
over the eastern Pacific looks to eject early next week and travel 
overtop the western/central US ridge axis, cresting the ridge early 
next week and looking to make a beeline for the Upper Midwest going 
through the first half of the week. Quite a bit of uncertainty yet 
in the timing of this feature, and how the situation evolves beyond 
that...but think we could remain unsettled and perhaps a touch cool 
(depending on how strong troughing ends up in our region) going into 
the middle of next week. 

FORECAST DETAILS...

Rain/storm chances today...While the PV max will approach us later 
today...do think that it will struggle to produce much given dry air 
in the lower levels and a mid-level inversion around 600mb (ish) 
that should keep most, if not all, activity capped. The best shot 
for anything to develop would be across the EUP where the better 
moisture and forcing would be located today, though suppose it's not 
out of the question some showers could pop along the Lake Huron lake 
breeze in northeast Lower. Additionally, noting a smoke plume aloft 
drifting in late yesterday, do wonder if this could further limit 
diurnal heating potential and thus, instability potential as well. 

Rain/storm chances tonight/Friday...expect rain/storms should 
increase from the west/northwest through the night, esp across the 
Yoop, closer to the better moisture aloft and better forcing, and 
expect an uptick in activity especially after 6z. Appears there is 
some marginal deep-layer shear over the region tonight, though 
unclear attm if this will have any bearing on showers/storms 
tonight. Otherwise, showers/storms should slowly progress eastward 
through the day Friday, though some guidance soundings suggest it 
may take most of the day to saturate the lower levels, which could 
slow rain chances and diminish QPF to some degree, though not 
impossible some rain could make it to the ground out of a 7-10kft 
cloud deck. There are some hints attm for an area of theta-e 
advection across central Lower MI into northeast Lower MI ahead of 
the approaching PV max. Do wonder if these are signals for some 
showers and storms to develop well out ahead of the primary cold 
front, even as early as 8-10z Friday morning, with signals for some 
elevated instability to crop up prior to daytime heating. This area 
of more unstable air across NE Lower seems to persist into the 
afternoon, which could keep this area at risk for showers/storms for 
much of the day, especially into the afternoon as lake breezes could 
take shape. Most likely, QPF totals thru Friday evening should be 
generally under a half inch, but would not be out of the question if 
some area sat longer under rain and ended up with a bit more. This 
idea carries into Saturday as well.
